chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah who said:

I asked him (peace be upon him) about the man who buys a slave while he is an absconder from his family. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'It is not valid except if he buys another thing along with it, so he would say, 'I buy from you this thing and your slave for such and such.' So if he is not able to take the slave, the price he paid is considered for the thing.'

key_terms.آبِق: An absconder or runaway slave who hides from his master

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling for buying a slave who is currently hiding or absent?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the fiqh of 'shurut al-abiq' (conditioning the purchase on the slave's presence) to mitigate risk in transactions involving an absent or runaway slave. By bundling the slave with another commodity, the buyer secures a fallback asset, reflecting the Shia scholarly emphasis on preventing uncertainty (gharar) and ensuring equitable compensation in commercial law.
